title: Plan-then-execute supervision
description: The coordinator first produces a step plan and validates it against policy before any tool runs. Each step names its tool, inputs, and expected output shape. Execution then follows the approved plan; deviations require re-planning. This separates thinking from doing. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers approving a step plan before execution.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 3, 2: 5, 3: 8}
N = CFG[LEVEL]
plan = [{"step": i, "tool": "tool-%d" % (i % 3), "expects": "record"} for i in range(1, N + 1)]
policy_ok = all(p["tool"].startswith("tool-") for p in plan)
print("plan steps:", N, "| policy valid:", policy_ok, "| executing:", policy_ok)

title: Stepwise validation gates
description: Each step's output passes through a validation gate before the next step begins: schema checks, value ranges, and cross-field consistency. A failed gate halts the pipeline with the offending output attached, instead of letting bad data poison downstream steps. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers gating each step's output on schema and ranges.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: [10, 20, -5], 2: [10, 20, 30, -5], 3: [10, 20, 30, 40, -5, 60]}
outputs = CFG[LEVEL]
def gate(v): return isinstance(v, int) and v >= 0
halted = None
for i, v in enumerate(outputs):
    if not gate(v): halted = (i, v); break
print("outputs:", outputs, "| halted at:", halted or "none - all gates passed")
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Timeout and watchdog supervision
description: Every step gets a deadline, and a watchdog aborts steps that exceed it. Timeouts distinguish slow steps (retry with more time) from stuck steps (abort and escalate). Watchdog events are logged with the step's partial progress for diagnosis. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers per-step deadlines with abort.

title: Result reconciliation
description: When a task fans out to parallel steps, the coordinator reconciles the partial results: checking coverage (did every shard report?), consistency (do overlapping results agree?), and completeness. Missing or conflicting partials trigger targeted re-runs instead of full restarts. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers checking coverage across parallel partials.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: {"shards": 4, "got": 4}, 2: {"shards": 8, "got": 7}, 3: {"shards": 16, "got": 14}}
shards, got = CFG[LEVEL]["shards"], CFG[LEVEL]["got"]
missing = shards - got
print("shards %d/%d reported" % (got, shards), "| missing:", missing, "| action:", "reconcile ok" if not missing else "re-run %d shards" % missing)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Compensation on failure (saga)
description: For multi-step tasks without atomic transactions, each step registers a compensating action that undoes it. If a later step fails, the coordinator runs compensations in reverse order, unwinding the partial work. The saga log records every forward and compensating action. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers registering compensating actions per step.
